deckTitle: Intensive Care Medicine: The Vital Vigil

cards.power: The Wet-Lung-Wallop. Axe floods the alveoli with protein-rich Sludge, turning the lungs into stiff, unexpandable Stone.
cards.lore: Cytokine-driven damage to the alveolar-capillary barrier creates Baby Lungs — small patches of functional tissue in a sea of collapse.
cards.gradeReason: Clear villain but more describes pathology than invites immediate embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Angry axe-wielding bear floods lung alveoli with sludge. Style: MedKayfab sketchbook. Mood: destructive and clinical.

cards.power: The Balloon-Support. Keeps the tiny Alveolar-Balloons from snapping shut at the end of every breath.
cards.lore: Increases Functional Residual Capacity. Caveat: Too much PEEP crushes the Heart-Pump (Decreases Preload).
cards.gradeReason: Balloon-Support is instantly visual — you know exactly what to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cheerful hedgehog propping open tiny lung balloons. Style: MedKayfab watercolor. Mood: supportive and precise.

cards.power: The Over-Stretch. Pushes too much air into too little lung, tearing tissue apart.
cards.lore: Volutrauma and Barotrauma. Turn Protective-Ventilation into Destructive-Air-Hammer.
cards.gradeReason: Villain role is clear but Over-Stretch needs a moment of clinical context to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Gorilla over-inflating pink lung balloon until it tears. Style: MedKayfab crosshatch. Mood: reckless and violent.

cards.power: The Gravity-Flip. Let the Back-Lungs breathe while the Front-Lungs rest.
cards.lore: Homogenizes and strain. Moves the weight of the heart and get off the dorsal alveoli to improve the Ventilation-Perfusion-Match.
cards.gradeReason: Gravity-Flip is kinetic and physical — you know immediately what to do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Raccoon flipping patient prone, lungs glowing from the back. Style: MedKayfab action. Mood: dynamic and lifesaving.

cards.power: The Pressure-Anchor. Clamps the leaky Peripheral-Pipes to ensure the Brain-and-Heart-Vaults stay pressurized.
cards.lore: The Vasopressor of Choice. Increases MAP without over-revving the heart-engine.
cards.gradeReason: Pressure-Anchor is immediate and powerful — no explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Stoic owl clamping pipe network to prevent leaks, MAP display rising. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: authoritative and steady.

cards.power: The Piston-Push. Screams at the failing heart-engine to squeeze harder.
cards.lore: Used in Cardiogenic-Carl. Caveat: It's a vasodilator — he might drop the MAP while boosting the flow.
cards.gradeReason: Piston-Push at a failing engine — instantly performative and charged.
cards.artworkPrompt: Electric cheetah punching failing heart engine, cardiac output arrows exploding. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: urgent and explosive.

cards.power: The Real-Time-Radar. Gives the Beat-by-Beat truth, profiling every Pulse-Pressure-Variation.
cards.lore: Allows for frequent blood gases. If the waveform Dampens, the Archer is hitting a wall or pipes are kinked.
cards.gradeReason: Real-Time-Radar is evocative, but arterial line as archer needs a moment of context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Fox archer shooting arrow into radial artery, waveform trail behind. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: precise and continuous.

cards.power: The Deep-Diver. Swims through the heart into the lungs to see the pressure in the Left-Atrium-Lobby.
cards.lore: Differentiates Heart-Failure-Flood from Septic-Leak. Rare now, but essential for Complex-Cases.
cards.gradeReason: Deep-Diver metaphor is vivid; PAC complexity means non-specialists need context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Swan diving through cardiac chambers to pulmonary artery, wedge pressure displayed. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: elegant and rare.

cards.power: The 24-Hour-Sieve. Slowly cleans the blood, removing Toxin-Tokens without crashing the blood pressure.
cards.lore: Gentle. Mimics the natural kidney for wrestlers who are too unstable for a fast Flush.
cards.gradeReason: 24-Hour-Sieve is clear, but CRRT as a character needs its gradual pace established first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Patient tortoise sifting blood through slow sieve filter, toxins captured. Style: MedKayfab sketchbook. Mood: methodical and gentle.

cards.power: The Electrical-Eraser. Shorts out the heart's wiring, leading to the Sine-Wave-Silence.
cards.lore: Stops the resting membrane potential. Treat with Calcium-the-Shield to protect wires, then Insulin-the-Evictor.
cards.gradeReason: Electrical-Eraser shorting a heart — maximum menace, zero ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Jellyfish villain erasing heart's electrical wiring with peaked T-waves. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: lethal and electric.

cards.power: The Protein-Malter. Turns the blood sour, causing Pressor-Ponies to stop and the heart to stumble.
cards.lore: A sign of Tissue-Starvation. If the cells can't breathe, they vomit acid. A signal of Energy-Failure.
cards.gradeReason: Protein-Malter is inventive but abstract — needs slight context for embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Acid rhinoceros melting protein structures in bloodstream, pH dropping. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: corrosive and ominous.

cards.power: The Machine-Shield. Eats the calcium in the dialysis circuit so blood doesn't Clot-the-Filter.
cards.lore: Regional means it only works inside the machine. Caveat: If the liver can't process it, causes Calcium-Crashing.
cards.gradeReason: Functional character but highly technical — only performative to those running CRRT.
cards.artworkPrompt: Armadillo gobbling calcium ions inside dialysis tubing, filter staying clean. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: technical and protective.

cards.power: The Capillary-Collapse. Opens all Volume-Valves and turns vessel-walls into Leaky-Cheese.
cards.lore: Immune-overdrive causes massive vasodilation. Blood hides in Peripheral-Puddles, leaving the brain dry.
cards.gradeReason: Leaky-Cheese villain with blood hiding in puddles — pure performative chaos.
cards.artworkPrompt: Flaming rat punching open vessel walls, blood pooling in puddles. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: systemic riot and mayhem.

cards.power: The Bacterial-Beacon. Glows bright when Bacterial-Punks are in the blood, dim for Viral-Vandals.
cards.lore: Guides when to start — and when to stop — the Antibiotic-Artillery.
cards.gradeReason: Bacterial-Beacon is clear, but the biomarker role is guidance, not immediate performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Glowing firefly illuminating bacterial invaders in bloodstream, dim near viruses. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: diagnostic and selective.

cards.power: The Hypoxia-Tax. Represents the Oxygen-Debt from failing aerobic metabolism.
cards.lore: High Lactate = Tissue Ischemia. Clearing the Lactate proves the Resuscitation-Rescue is winning.
cards.gradeReason: Debt-Collector collecting Hypoxia-Tax — the metaphor sings immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Suited debt-collector bear counting oxygen receipts from starving tissue. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: ominous and accountable.

cards.power: The Root-Removal. Knows that Antibiotic-Ammo fails if the Nest isn't destroyed.
cards.lore: Ibi pus, ibi evacuo. (If there is pus, drain it). If the line is dirty, pull it.
cards.gradeReason: Root-Removal with Latin battle cry — you know exactly what to do and why.
cards.artworkPrompt: Surgeon warrior extracting infected nest from battlefield, pus draining out. Style: MedKayfab action. Mood: decisive and surgical.

cards.power: The Skull-Squeeze. Swelling brain crushes the Oxygen-Entry-Vessels.
cards.lore: The skull is a Closed-Box. If ICP reaches MAP, the Brain-Death-Bell rings.
cards.gradeReason: Skull-Squeeze is vivid; ICP as character sits more as threat-descriptor than role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Brain swelling pressing against skull walls, oxygen vessels crushed. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: claustrophobic and deadly.

cards.power: The Water-Sucker. Pulls water out of swollen brain-tissue and into the blood.
cards.lore: Creates an Osmotic-Gradient. Caveat: Mannitol causes Diuresis-Drain, 3% Saline keeps volume in pipes.
cards.gradeReason: Redundant name kills the character; 'Osmotic-the-Osmotic' is a naming convention failure.
cards.artworkPrompt: Crab siphoning water out of swollen brain tissue into bloodstream. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: technical and dehydrating.

cards.power: The Mainframe-Mute. Puts the brain to sleep and covers the Oxygen-Burn-Rate.
cards.lore: Allows the Daily-Wake-Up-Test. Caveat: PRIS (Infusion Syndrome) causes acidosis and heart failure.
cards.gradeReason: The Milk nickname is legendary in medicine — instant character, instant performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: White sheep pouring milky sedation into IV line, brain powering down softly. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: serene and potent.

cards.power: The Conscious-Calm. Provides Analgo-Sedation — sleepy but can answer the Neuro-Check.
cards.lore: Doesn't stop the breathing-drive. Great for Ventilator-Weaning. Caveat: Can cause Brady-Bill (Slow heart).
cards.gradeReason: Conscious-Calm is good; alpha-2 mechanism means specialists recognise it faster.
cards.artworkPrompt: Sloth in scrubs nodding sleepily but answering questions, breathing normally. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: calm and cooperative.

cards.power: The Vein-Feed. Bypasses the Gut-Gate to feed directly through the blood.
cards.lore: The Last Resort. TPN loves the Liver-Limp and Line-Infection-Ingles. If the gut works, use the gut!
cards.gradeReason: Vein-Feed is clear; the parenteral/parental pun needs parsing and card is functional not knockout.
cards.artworkPrompt: Hummingbird feeding nutrients directly into central line, gut gate bypassed and closed. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: reluctant and risky.

cards.power: The Acid-Erosion. Eats the stomach lining during the Stress-Storm, causing a Hidden-Bleed.
cards.lore: Prevented by PPI-the-Lock or H2-the-Hinderer.
cards.gradeReason: Shadow-villain concept is strong but the one-line lore deflates the card's tension.
cards.artworkPrompt: Shadow rat gnawing stomach lining during ICU storm, hidden bleeding below. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: covert and corrosive.

cards.power: The Static-Snake. Intestines stop moving, causing Belly-Bloat and Vomitus-Vex.
cards.lore: Often caused by Opioid-Overload or Electrolyte-Emptying.
cards.gradeReason: Static-Snake on strike with HUMBUG sticker — the gut-strike framing is immediate and comic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Lazy snake curled on intestines holding ON STRIKE sign, belly bloating above. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: idle and obstructive.

cards.power: The Detox-Failure. Stops cleaning the blood, letting Ammonia-the-Fog cloud the brain.
cards.lore: Watch for Cerebral-Edema-Swelling. It is a race for the Transplant-Train.
cards.gradeReason: Detox-Failure with Ammonia-Fog is clear; the race metaphor adds urgency but role stays descriptive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Closed opossum factory leaking ammonia fog into brain above. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: toxic and urgent.

cards.power: The Clot-and-Bleed. Uses up all Clot-Tokens in tiny, useless fights, leaving nothing for Major-Leaks.
cards.lore: A Consumption-Coagulopathy. Treat the underlying Sam-Sepsis to stop the spiral.
cards.gradeReason: Clot-and-Bleed paradox is instantly graspable and dramatically absurd.
cards.artworkPrompt: Porcupine clotting everywhere uselessly while massive hemorrhage goes untreated. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: paradoxical and catastrophic.

cards.power: The Hole-Stoppage. The first line of defense against Capillary-Leaks.
cards.lore: In the ICU, Plugs get eaten by Sam-Sepsis and Spleen-the-Sponge.
cards.gradeReason: Hole-Stoppage is functional; the puppy platelet artwork is charming but character identity is thin.
cards.artworkPrompt: Tiny golden puppy platelet squad plugging capillary hole, sepsis monster eating them. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: earnest and overwhelmed.

cards.power: The Liquid-Gold. Restores the Coagulation-Cascade when the INR-Alarm is ringing.
cards.lore: Essential for Wart-Reversal and Massive-Hemorrhage.
cards.gradeReason: Liquid-Gold is good but character identity is thinner than DIC or TEG cards.
cards.artworkPrompt: Golden plasma bag flooding broken coagulation cascade waterfall back to life. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: restorative and golden.

cards.power: The Real-Time-Clot-Movie. Tells exactly why blood isn't clotting: Factor-Failure, Platelet-Pouchy, or Fibrin-Frenzy.
cards.lore: Guided Goat-Directed-Therapy. Don't guess — TEG it!
cards.gradeReason: Real-Time-Clot-Movie is a brilliant image; TEG itself is niche enough to require specialist context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Spider on viscoelastic web displaying clot formation graph in real time. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: precise and diagnostic.

cards.power: The Vessel-Sensitizer. Helps the Norad-Pressor work better by making vessels sensitive to the signal.
cards.lore: Replaces Relative-Adrenal-Insufficiency.
cards.gradeReason: Vessel-Sensitizer is accurate but the supporting-actor role is harder to embody than leads.
cards.artworkPrompt: Meerkat tuning vessel antenna to norepinephrine signal, MAP stabilizing. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: supportive and sensitizing.

cards.power: The Calcium-Cutter. Stops the Muscle-Meltdown in Malignant Hyperthermia.
cards.lore: Prevents the runaway release of calcium from the Sarcoplastic-Silo.
cards.gradeReason: Inferno-Cooler name alone is a complete performance invitation — you are the firefighter.
cards.artworkPrompt: Firefighter penguin hosing down exploding muscle furnace, temperature dropping fast. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: emergency and cooling.

cards.power: The Muscle-Wake-Up. Grabs Paralyzer-Punks and drags them away from the Nerve-Junction.
cards.lore: Immediate reversal of neuromuscular blockade. No Wet-Side Effects like Neostigmine.
cards.gradeReason: Grabs Paralyzer-Punks and drags them away — the action is specific, vivid, and physical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Vacuum cleaner character sucking paralyzer particles from neuromuscular junction, muscles awakening. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: swift and decisive.

cards.power: The Surgical-Calm. The go-to for continuous Analgesia-Infusion in the ventilated wrestler.
cards.lore: Rapid onset. Caveat: Causes Chest-Wall-Rigidity-DIFF if pushed too fast.
cards.gradeReason: Surgical-Calm is good; chest-wall-rigidity caveat is specialist knowledge that anchors it to G2.
cards.artworkPrompt: Black panther moving silently, pain waves dissolving in its wake. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: fast and potent.

cards.power: The Physiological-Fill. The Gold Standard for filling the Septic-Tank.
cards.lore: Closer to blood than Normal-Saline-the-Salty, which can cause Chloride-Acid-Abyss.
cards.gradeReason: Gold Standard Septic-Tank-filler is functional; fluid characters are harder to embody theatrically.
cards.artworkPrompt: Balanced frog filling tank with physiological fluid, electrolyte crystals glowing green. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: steady and restorative.

cards.power: The Water-Magnet. Stays in the Pipe-Highway and pulls fluid out of the Tissue-Swamps (Edema).
cards.lore: Used when crystalloids fail or after large-volume Ascites-Draining.
cards.gradeReason: Water-Magnet is strong; colloid character is clear but less theatrical than leading cards.
cards.artworkPrompt: Protein magnet pulling swamp water back into blood vessel highway. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: attractive and expensive.

cards.power: The Squeeze-Out. Removes the Extra-Weight post-shock to let the lungs breathe.
cards.lore: Lasix-the-Lasix is the main tool. Being Too-Wet increases the Ventilator-Time.
cards.gradeReason: Squeeze-Out camel is vivid; the dry-down role is clear but reactive rather than proactive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Camel wringing excess fluid from lung sponge, ventilator timer ticking. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: pragmatic and dehydrating.

cards.power: The Fluid-Challenge-Without-Fluid. Tells if the heart wants more volume before you pour it in.
cards.lore: The Reversible-Auto-Transfusion. If MAP goes up, the heart is Fluid-Responsive.
cards.gradeReason: Fluid-Challenge-Without-Fluid is conceptually knockout — the paradox demands immediate performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Hippo lifting legs 45 degrees, stroke volume arrows shooting upward, WHOOSH. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: diagnostic and reversible.

cards.power: The Emergency-Return. When the Golden-Tube is removed too early and the Airway-Assassins return.
cards.lore: High-risk move. Swelling (Edema) makes the second pass much harder than the first.
cards.gradeReason: Panic is in the name and stakes are clear; the role is situational more than characterful.
cards.artworkPrompt: Octopus emergency re-inserting golden tube into collapsing airway, swelling closing in. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: urgent and high-stakes.

cards.power: The Machine-Induced-Crush. The ventilator Pops a lung-blob, squeezing the heart.
cards.lore: Always disconnect the vent first in sudden PEA to rule out Auto-PEEP or Tension-Tony.
cards.gradeReason: Disconnect the vent first — the lore is the most actionable single sentence in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Inflated lung squeezing cartoon heart sideways, ventilator cord to be cut. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: crushing and immediate.

cards.power: The Clot-Irony. Makes platelets clump together while numbers drop, causing Venous-and-Arterial-Jams.
cards.lore: Immune-mediated riot. Stop Heparin immediately and use Argatroban-the-Alternative.
cards.gradeReason: Clot-Irony is a clever concept; the paradox needs explaining before it can be performed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Fox hunting platelets while clots form in veins, heparin bottles crossed out. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: ironic and urgent.

cards.power: The Highway-Block. A clot-monster from the Leg-Deep-Veins jams the Lung-Entrance.
cards.lore: In the ICU, the Phantom is often completely silent until it is too late.
cards.gradeReason: Completely silent until too late — the Phantom earns its grade through menace and inevitability.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ghost clot monster blocking lung highway, arriving silently from deep veins below. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: silent and lethal.

cards.power: The Machine-Breach. Bacterial-Punks crawl down the Golden-Tube to start a riot.
cards.lore: Prevented by Head-Up-Position and Oral-Chlorhexidine-Cloe.
cards.gradeReason: Machine-Breach is clear; prevention-focused lore deflates the villain's menace.
cards.artworkPrompt: Bacteria marching down ventilator tube into lung riot zone below. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: infiltrating and preventable.

cards.power: The IV-Invasion. Staph-the-Skin-Steward enters the Blood-Highway through the CVC-Portal.
cards.lore: Scrub the Hub! If the line is infected, it must be Evicted.
cards.gradeReason: Scrub the Hub lore is a knockout line; the card itself is more procedure than embodied character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Staph bacterium in suit sliding through central line hub into bloodstream. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: invasive and evictable.

cards.power: The Gut-Explosion. Takes over the Bowel-Basement after Antibiotic-Artillery kills the good guards.
cards.lore: Smells like a Horse-Barn. Treat with Vanomy-the-Vault (Oral).
cards.gradeReason: Smells like a Horse-Barn is the most memorable single lore line in the deck. Unmistakable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Spore-crowned villain taking over bowel kingdom, horse-barn stench rising in clouds. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: opportunistic and odorous.

cards.power: The Armor-Plated-Punks. Multidrug-Resistance shields laugh at standard Antibiotic-Ammo.
cards.lore: They use Efflux-Pumps and Enzyme-Blasters (Carbapenemases) to survive.
cards.gradeReason: Armor-Plated-Punks is excellent; six-organism acronym requires specialist recognition.
cards.artworkPrompt: Six armored bacteria warriors laughing at antibiotic arrows bouncing harmlessly off them. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: resistant and menacing.

cards.power: The Test-Drive. The machine steps back, letting the wrestler breathe alone for 30-120 mins.
cards.lore: Passes if the Heart-Rate and Work-of-Breathing remain stable and low.
cards.gradeReason: Test-Drive with the wrestler breathing alone — the wrestling frame pays off perfectly here.
cards.artworkPrompt: Robot stepping back as wrestler bird breathes alone on test mat, RSBI dial low. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: tense and hopeful.

cards.power: The Hallucination-Haze. Makes the wrestler see Shadow-Monsters and pull at their tubes.
cards.lore: Caused by Sleep-Sabotage, Benzodiazepine-Bouncers, and Sam-Sepsis.
cards.gradeReason: Pull at their tubes — anyone who has seen ICU delirium recognises this instantly and viscerally.
cards.artworkPrompt: Chameleon wrestler hallucinating shadow monsters, pulling at IV tubes in confusion. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: hallucinatory and distressing.

cards.power: The Long-Shadow. The wrestler remains weak and forgetful for months after leaving the Vital-Vigil.
cards.lore: ICU-Acquired-Weakness. The muscles melted away during the long sleep.
cards.gradeReason: Clinically vital but post-discharge syndrome is harder to perform at the table than acute events.
cards.artworkPrompt: Weak turtle shuffling out of ICU, muscles wasted, memory fog surrounding outside. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: lingering and sobering.

cards.power: The Peaceful-Exit. When the Scrimmage is lost, focus shifts to a Quiet-Mat without pain.
cards.lore: Withdrawal of Life-Sustaining Treatment. Morphine and Midazolam ensure the final breath is soft.
cards.gradeReason: The final breath is soft — the most profound card in any MedKayfab deck. No explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Swan guiding wrestler to quiet peaceful mat, pain dissolving in soft warm light. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: tender and dignified.

cards.power: The Main-Line. Allows for Pressor-Pumps, TPN-Feeding, and Fast-Fluid-Filling.
cards.lore: Allows CVP monitoring. Caveat: Watch for Pneumo-the-Puncture during placement.
cards.gradeReason: Cavalry metaphor is apt; the triple-lumen catheter role is primarily logistical not theatrical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Squid cavalry charging with triple-lumen catheter lance through subclavian access. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: procedural and reliable.

cards.power: The Organ-Perfusion-Monitor. Tells the surgeon if Kidney-Filters are getting enough Blood.
cards.lore: Oliguria-the-Small-Flow is the very first sign of Shock-Sam.
cards.gradeReason: Oliguria is the first sign of Shock — this lore carries the weight of a clinical rule that saves lives.
cards.artworkPrompt: Guard on hourly watch at urinary output meter, shock warning bell ready to ring. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: vigilant and sentinel.

cards.power: The Panic-Drain. When the body's filters fail completely and the AEIOU-Alarms ring.
cards.lore: High potassium or pulmonary edema that won't respond to Lasix requires the machine NOW.
cards.gradeReason: AEIOU-Alarms is a strong mnemonic hook; the emergency role is clear but list-driven.
cards.artworkPrompt: Demon on AEIOU keyboard triggering dialysis emergency, alarms flashing red. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: emergency and overwhelming.

cards.power: The Ultimate-Bypass. Takes blood outside the body, gasses it with oxygen, and pumps it back.
cards.lore: The Highest-Level-Support. Buys weeks of time for the biological heart or lungs to heal.
cards.gradeReason: Ultimate-Bypass — the finality and scale of ECMO makes this immediately epic to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Massive whale oxygenating blood outside glowing patient body, time purchased. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: ultimate and extraordinary.

cards.power: The Meta-Physiologist.
cards.lore: Is the CO2 rising? Is the MAP holding? Is the Lactate clearing? Balance the system! Stay fluffy!
cards.gradeReason: Stay fluffy! The meta-card that makes you want to BE the attending running everything at once.
cards.artworkPrompt: Multi-armed rabbit doctor managing monitors, vents, and labs simultaneously. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: omnipresent and fluffy.

cards.power: The Acid-Blockade.
cards.lore: Identify the Sensitivity-Tool to help pressors work (Hydrocort-Support) and the Brain-Tool for the acid (CRRT-the-Constant).
cards.gradeReason: Clinical puzzle card — clear challenge but answer-hunting is different from embodied play.
cards.artworkPrompt: FrizzleBob quest map showing septic pH trap with two hidden solution tools marked. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: puzzle and urgent.

cards.power: The Air-Trap.
cards.lore: Identify the Machine-Induced-Killer (Tension-the-Tony). The very first move: Disconnect the Vent!
cards.gradeReason: Disconnect the Vent — the most actionable clinical instruction in the deck, delivered as a quest.
cards.artworkPrompt: FrizzleBob quest: PEA alarm, gorilla hand reaching for ventilator disconnect switch. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: crisis and decisive.

cards.power: The Sarcoplasmic-Fire.
cards.lore: Identify the Inland-Inferno (Malignant Hyperthermia) and deploy the Calcium-Cutter (Dantrolene-the-Inferno-Cooler).
cards.gradeReason: Inland-Inferno is vivid; the OR scenario needs specialist setup before it lands.
cards.artworkPrompt: FrizzleBob quest in OR, 41C thermometer and rigid muscle monster awaiting dantrolene. Style: MedKayfab. Mood: rare and fiery.

verdict: The Vital Vigil is the strongest single-specialty MedKayfab deck so far — ICU medicine was born for this format. Named strength: Comfort-Care-the-Transition is the most emotionally resonant card in the corpus; Tension-the-Tony's lore ('Disconnect the Vent first') is a life-saving instruction dressed as a wrestling move. Named weakness: Osmotic-the-Osmotic breaks the naming convention with a redundant double-name, and PICS-the-Post-ICU-Struggle is educationally vital but theatrically thin. The three Quest cards on page 15 turn the deck into a clinical scenario engine. Table-ready YES.
blurb: 56 ICU wrestling cards where Septic-Sam bleeds the system dry and Comfort-Care-the-Transition closes the match with dignity. For medical students, residents, and anyone who wants to feel the ICU before they step inside.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — Multi-armed rabbit intensivist surrounded by ventilators and monitors in chaotic ICU cartoon panorama; immediately sets tone.
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'The Vital Vigil' is one of the best deck subtitles in the corpus — poetic and precise.
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Life on the threshold between existence and void; cover delivers exactly what the cards contain.
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — Strong but the ICU cartoon aesthetic is now recognizable across the MedKayfab series.
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — Highly shareable in medical communities; broader audience needs more context.
coverQA.coverNote: This cover earns a 5 on three of five dimensions. 'Titrating the threshold between life and the void. Stay fluffy!' is FrizzleBob at his best. The ICU machinery in the background rewards close inspection. The 'Call Doc Frizzle!' corner callout is a nice meta-hook for the attending card on page 15.

notes: 15 pages: 1 cover + 14 story pages x 4 cards = 56 cards. Layout: 2x2 grid throughout. Page headers alternate 'The $abotaged $ketchbook' (dollar-sign Ss) and plain 'The Sabotaged Sketchbook'. Special stickers on pages 8 (KaytaBINGO!), 9 (KayfaBOGGLE!), 10 (What the FLUFF?), 11 (Call Doc Frizzle!), 13 (Stay Fluffy!), 14 (Diagnosis?!). No RAF dice boxes visible. Page 15 is a FrizzleBob meta-page with ICU Attending + 3 Quest scenario cards. 'Wart-Reversal' in FFP lore = warfarin reversal; 'Goat-Directed-Therapy' in TEG lore = goal-directed therapy. PICS card artwork is notably more subdued/grayscale than other cards — intentional tonal shift. Subfolder path 'MedKayfab MegaPack/' omitted from sourceFile per convention.

urgent: Rename 'Osmotic-the-Osmotic' — redundant name breaks naming convention; candidate: 'Hyperton-the-Hypertonic' or 'Mannitol-the-Mindwipe'
quickWins: Beef up PICS card power text to be more performative
Add second lore line to Stress-Ulcer-the-Shadow — currently thin
niceToHave: Consider POCUS/Ultrasound card — now standard ICU tool
Quest cards could include difficulty rating
